_meta.note: Canonical schema for .planning/config.json. Source of truth for keys, types, enums, and defaults. Validated by bin/config.mjs; the cad-config walk reads each setting's question and value explanations from it (see `walk`). `src` is CONFIG-LAYER SCOPE, not enum provenance: [repo] = settable in either layer; [global] = the user-global layer only, and a repo layer setting it is stripped at the merge and named in the read face's warnings (bin/lib/global-only-keys.mjs, cross-checked against this field by self-verify in both directions); absent = repo-settable. `repo_only` is a DIFFERENT and much narrower marker than `src`, and the two are read separately: present and `true` means only that repository's own .planning/config.json can set the key, so bin/config.mjs REFUSES a write aimed at the user-global layer at write time rather than stripping it at the merge; absent means either layer, which is every other key. The test it encodes, for a maintainer deciding whether a new key qualifies: would a user-global value AUTHORIZE a change to a repository that never opted in? If yes the key is `repo_only`; a key that merely has a sensible per-repo value is not. Every key carries a `section`, one of six groups named by what you are trying to do (Models and effort, When reviews run, Who reviews, Testing, Git and landing, How work runs); a key with a `section` and no `question` is Advanced, which means it is listed with its `purpose` under that group, is not asked in the walk and does not count toward a group's 16 shown settings. `applies_when` is an OPTIONAL list of conditions that must ALL hold for the setting to do anything, each a `key` plus exactly one of `not`, `is` or `includes`, compared by deep equality against the value in force (the layer value, else the schema default; the merged config holds no defaults, so an unset gate would pass `not: off`). `not` and `is` take a whole value, and `includes` asks whether a list value holds one member. A failed condition makes the read say the setting has no effect and why, and a condition naming a key the schema does not hold is refused by self-verify. It sits on the eight review.triggers.<t>.tier and .effort keys and on roles.cad-mapper.model and .effort only; any other rule stays a sentence. `interacts` is OPTIONAL free text for what a setting depends on that no condition can read, such as a needed second config file or a host setting, and the menu prints it under Works with.
_meta.types: bool | int | string | string_or_null | enum | array_string | array_enum. int accepts an optional 'min'. enum/array_enum carry 'values'. `grammar` is an OPTIONAL further narrowing of a value whose type already passed, naming one predicate in the frozen GRAMMARS registry of bin/lib/config-value.mjs: the type says what kind of value this is, the grammar says which of those values this key serves. It is evaluated at the write face (set/check) and over a whole file (validate), a null value skips it because null means the question was never asked, and a marker naming a predicate the registry does not hold is an error rather than a silent pass - a key claiming a grammar nothing enforces is the failure the marker exists to prevent.
_meta.walk: OPTIONAL per-key fields that carry the /cad-config walk's text, so the walk and any other reader (a config panel) take it from this one file. `question` is the sentence the walk asks, and its presence marks the key as part of the walk; a key without it is not asked about. `section` names the group the key sits under and `position` is its 1-based place in the walk, which is not schema order. `explain` is a list of `{value, text}` entries, one per selectable answer: `value` keeps its real JSON type (a string, `true`, `false` or `null`) because an object keyed by value could only hold strings, and `text` is optional, so a bare entry is an answer with no gloss. Every explained value must be one the key accepts, with one exception: a `null` entry on a list key whose default is `null` explains the unset state, `set` refuses it, and a reader must not offer it as an answer. `hint` is a free-typed shape (a number, a shell command, a path, a comma list) and is never a selectable value, so a reader must not offer it as an option. `purpose` stays the key's reference text and is not the question. `label` is a few plain words that name the setting, on every key including the ones with no question, and unique within its `section`. The menu shows it in list rows in place of the dotted key, the `layers` reads and `catalog` return it, and a reader takes it from there and never composes one. `bin/config.mjs keys --walk` returns only the keys that hold a question, in `position` order, and leaves `label` off.

workflow.max_plan_tasks.purpose: Task ceiling PER PLAN, not per phase - a phase needing more capacity gets MORE PLANS, sequential where they share files, and `## PHASE TOO BIG` is returned only when no number of plans of that size can deliver the phase, which is a statement about the PHASE's scope and not about task count. The ceiling the planner is given up front, so an oversized plan is split rather than silently built. Re-decided 2026-08-17 against both of its forces and landing on 8, unchanged: cold-prefix cost - `weight.mjs resident` puts the executor's fixed dispatch prefix at 12,488 bytes, about 2% of a measured executor dispatch, so what an extra plan re-buys is the cold pass over the plan and the phase's artifacts rather than the prefix - and context risk - 15 executor checkpoints of 21 on this repo's `.planning/trace.jsonl`, every one of them from a plan already under this ceiling. v3.8.6:design-notes/dd-plan-task-ceiling.md carries the dated arithmetic

workflow.max_plan_bytes.purpose: Byte ceiling on what a SINGLE plan's `files:` frontmatter declares, measured as the sum of the on-disk sizes of those declared paths - PER PLAN and not per phase, the same reading workflow.max_plan_tasks carries, so a plan over it is split into MORE PLANS rather than shrunk in place. Those declared paths are what an executor dispatch is handed, and on one measured PLAN-1.md they were about 90% of a 70,554-token dispatch while nothing measured them against anything. A crossing is REPORTED and nothing is refused: plan-size report only (`bin/planning.mjs`), which workflows/plan.md hands the resolved value at its `check_size` step as `plan-size --max-bytes`; no dispatch path, agent frontmatter key or spawn seam consults it, so an over-ceiling plan is still planned and still executed. That is planning.max_capture_bullets's disposition and for its reason - the user may have authorized the full scope one step earlier, and a check that refused what they just authorized would be arguing with them. The default is the 75th percentile of the declared-byte distribution over this repository's 43 archived plans rounded UP to the next 25,000 (p25 207,298, p50 401,107, p75 667,580, p90 933,283, max 1,282,083, measured 2026-08-26; it fires on 10 of the 43), which is the derivation rule the six workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.* keys already state; references/config-reach.md carries the reach row

workflow.use_workflows.purpose: Run reviews as workflows: one agent per reviewer and one per finding, where the old path is one main session opening the file. Workflows burn usage fast (one measured review cost several times the single-session path in agent turns, 2026-11-05). It runs only when both config layers set it: the repository's .planning/config.json AND the user-global config must both be true, and either alone does nothing, so a committed repository value cannot turn on the costlier path for whoever clones it. Every reader goes through lib/workflow-layers.mjs's both-layer read (config.mjs workflow-layers), never a plain `get`. Each run takes exactly one path: the workflow path only with this on and the Workflow tool available, the old path otherwise.

When false, the default, /cad-config with no arguments opens the full walk as it did before the menu, and a sentence is not taken: it is answered with the command that turns this on, /cad-config workflow.config_menu=true. --walk, key=value and the guided flags work either way. /cad-config menu opening only

planning.code_map.purpose: Turn on the code map for planning. When true, /cad-plan and /cad-context each make one local scan with no model and add a short code map block to the agent's dispatch, and /cad-map can build and refresh the map. A true committed in a repository can only add that scan: no agent starts without a typed /cad-map and a yes. /cad-map obeys workflow-claim but not workflow.use_workflows. When false, the default, those dispatches carry nothing about a map and /cad-map answers with the command that turns this on, /cad-config planning.code_map=true. code map block and /cad-map only
planning.code_map.label: Code map for planning

planning.workflow_plans.purpose: Turn on plans a workflow can run. It works with planning.code_map off and gives thinner briefs. When false, the default, every path is as it was. workflow plans only

git.forge_provider.purpose: Which forge hosts this repository's issue tracker, resolved ONCE at project setup by /cad-new-project or /cad-adopt and read at land time in place of any host detection: bin/issue-check.mjs picks its provider row from this value rather than classifying the origin URL, so a repository that temporarily loses its remote does not silently change behaviour. Spelled with the same vocabulary bin/lib/issue-decision.mjs's HOST_TABLE uses for its rows. null means unasked - the setup step has not run or the user has not picked a provider yet. Settable in either config layer: naming which forge you use is a preference, and it authorizes nothing on a repository that never named ITSELF - binding a call to a repository is git.forge_repo's job, and that key is repo_only.

git.forge_repo.purpose: The owner/name slug this repository's forge calls address, resolved ONCE at project setup - offered as a default read off origin, confirmed by the user - and read at land time in place of any host detection, as bin/issue-check.mjs's --repo selector. null means unasked. repo_only: a user-global slug would point EVERY repository's forge calls at one target, which is exactly the authorization test _meta.note states, so only that repository's own .planning/config.json may set it.
git.forge_repo.question: What is this repository called on that service, as owner/name?

git.forge_host.purpose: The Forgejo instance host the user confirmed at setup, spelled `hostname` or `hostname:port` when the instance is not on its scheme's default port - the port a browser reaches the instance on, never an SSH port - resolved ONCE at project setup and read at land time in place of any host detection, where bin/issue-check.mjs turns it into the tea login NAME the call is made under. NEVER derived from the origin URL: on a split SSH endpoint the origin's host is the SSH hostname, not the instance the user reaches in a browser, which is the shape this repository itself has - so it is ASKED outright and confirmed. null on the github and gitlab providers, whose hosts are fixed, and null anywhere else means unasked. Settable in either config layer, for the same reason git.forge_provider is: naming which instance you work with is a preference and authorizes nothing on a repository that never named itself.

git.forge_host.hint: a host name, or hostname:port when the server isn't on the default port. Use your browser's port, never SSH's. Checked when you set it.

git.auto_close.purpose: Opt-in end-to-end close: cad-milestone/cad-land run audit -> tag -> PR -> merge -> reset with no per-step prompts, halting on a surviving blocker/high risk_surface finding. It runs only when both config layers set it: the repository's .planning/config.json AND the user-global config must both be true, and either alone does nothing. A user-global value cannot authorize a repository that never opted in (D-08), and a committed repository value cannot authorize an unattended push on a machine whose user never opted in (D-02). Every reader goes through lib/repo-auto-close.mjs's both-layer read: git-publish.mjs publish and authorized, land-cleanup.mjs gate, and /cad-land step 3 and /cad-milestone step 7, which both branch on git-publish.mjs authorized.
git.auto_close.question: Close a cycle with no prompts, from audit to merge? This repository's config and your user-global config must both set it.

explain.text: run it start to finish, stopping only for an unresolved serious review finding
stop before publishing; you run /cad-land yourself

git.auto_close.interacts: It runs only when this repository's config and your user-global config both set it, so a value in one file alone does nothing.
git.auto_close.label: Close a cycle without prompts

planning.max_capture_bullets.purpose: Bound on the SUBSTANTIVE walked bullets .planning/CAPTURE.md may hold - the Todos, Seeds and Notes count with the `- None.` placeholder excluded, which is what `planning.mjs capture-check` reports. A crossing is REPORTED and nothing is refused, the same consequence workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.* carries and for the same reason: capture-check report only (`bin/planning.mjs`), no writer consults it, so /cad-capture and /cad-execute's open items keep filing at a queue that is over. The default is this repository's own live figure rounded up - 30 substantive walked bullets measured 2026-08-25 after the hand sweep - so the bound sits ABOVE a healthy tree and fires on GROWTH rather than on arrival, because a bound that reddens the day it ships teaches its reader to ignore it. What it is for: the hand sweep took this queue to zero on 2026-08-08 and it regrew to 276 walked items in sixteen days, because nothing measured it against anything. references/config-reach.md carries the reach row

review.triggers.risk_surface.waive_routi.purpose: Which surfaces may NOT raise this project's plan-time risk floor. The floor does exactly two things - it makes the plan review blocking and it turns the deep-verify pass on - and naming a surface here withholds BOTH for that surface. It waives neither review itself: the blocking risk_surface review still fires on the actual diff, and this key cannot turn it off. It moves no role's model and no role's start rung, because the floor does not move those either. Every waiver applied is named in the resolve's `reason` with the surface and the file it would have raised on. A surface that is NOT named still raises: waiving `secrets` on a phase that also touches `destructive` still gets the blocking plan review and the deep pass. Left unset it waives nothing, which is a different state from an empty answer for the same reason its `surfaces` sibling has no default array
review.triggers.risk_surface.waive_routi.question: Which risky areas should not make a phase's plan review blocking or turn on the deeper check? The review of the actual changes still runs.
review.triggers.risk_surface.waive_routi.hint: The same eight areas as the risky code categories. An area you leave out still makes the plan review blocking and turns on the deeper check.
review.triggers.risk_surface.waive_routi.label: Categories that skip the higher bar
